column1: # --- u04.l01 Mi familia (tener). Also new here, row in core.tsv: familia

column12: Hermanos: brothers, or brothers and sisters.
Hijos: sons, or children.
Also fiancé, and groom at a wedding.
Abuelos: grandparents.
Mi hermana mayor: my older sister.
Estoy casado and soy casado are both heard.
Tengo veinte años: I'm twenty. Tengo que...: I have to...

column1: # --- u04.l02 Mi casa es su casa (possessives). Also new here, rows in core.tsv: vivir, departamento, baño, vecino

column12: Not an apartment: that is un departamento.
Las dos y cuarto: a quarter past two.
Mexican homes keep the water tank and the laundry up here.

column5: to have (auxiliary); there is, there are (hay)
column12: Hay un baño. To say where it is: el baño está arriba.
Also a watering can.
In Spain an estufa is a heater.
Informal: el refri.
Pagar la luz: to pay the electric bill.
Many homes use a gas tank refilled by truck.
For the weather say hace calor; for yourself, tengo calor.
Se renta: for rent.

column1: # --- u04.l04 ¿Cómo es? (adjective agreement). Also new here, rows in core.tsv: bonito, nuevo, amable

column12: The everyday Mexican word; bajo is standard.
¡Joven!: how you call a waiter or a clerk.
For people, mayor is more polite.
Vendors call any light-skinned customer güero or güera.

column1: # --- supporting (no lesson introduces these; usable from Unit 4 on)

column12: Masculine: el problema. No hay problema.
Don Beto, don Toño: respect and warmth.

column5: Mrs.; Ms. (respectful, before a first name)
